blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Nine areas in Luzon and the Visayas were gripped by a dangerous heat index on Thursday amid the effects of the El Nino phenomenon, according to the state weather bureau. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) classifies as dangerous heat indices ranging from 42°C to 51°C due to increased risk of heat cramps and heat exhaustion, which could lead to heat stroke. The heat index on Thursday soared to 43°C in La Granja, La Carlota, Negros Occidental and Borongan, Eastern Samar.
